newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sends rice gift to food-starved North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sends rice gift to food-starved North Korea.

text.p: Vietnam, one of the world's biggest rice exporters, said on Tuesday it had given food-starved North Korea 10,000 tonnes of the commodity.

The official Vietnam News Agency said the gift would "help the government and people of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea overcome shortages of food" and supplemented an earlier gift of 3,000 tonnes.
North Korea is facing widespread and acute food shortages after several years of severe flooding and drought.
Vietnam said last week it expected to become the world's biggest exporter of rice after Thailand this year, with output exceeding three million tonnes.
Vietnam and North Korea are two of the world's surviving communist states but lingering residual solidarity was stretched by Hanoi's decision to normalise ties with South Korea in 1992.
In April Vietnam rejected a request from Pyongyang for more than 100,000 tonnes of rice because of what it said were concerns over payment.
